ap_psychology-m167.set_intro: A clinical psychologist wrote a case report about a woman in her thirties. Several times a month, without any warning, the woman suddenly felt overwhelming terror, a pounding heart, trembling, and shortness of breath that peaked within minutes. She worried constantly about when the next episode would happen and began avoiding exercise because it raised her heart rate. Between episodes she was not anxious about a specific object or social situation. The psychologist used a false name for the woman and changed identifying details in the report. The psychologist took an eclectic approach, using ideas from the cognitive and biological perspectives.
